title: Тост за вселенную и счёт за коньяк  (A Toast to the Universe and the Cognac Bill)

segments.t: Finishing his story in the office, Chef Barinov jokes to Lyova that swallowing the ring was not even a blunder—it was the universe itself trying to save Nagiyev from marrying Kristina. Out at the bar, meanwhile, Kostya hands Max the hefty bill for the expensive cognac they drank while swapping stories.
Я подумал.
Дело же не в нем.
Давай выпьем за нас.
За нас?
До дна.
Что это был косяк.
Потому что вся вселенная не хотела.
Чтобы хозяин женился на этой стерве.
А я сейчас серьезно говорю, между прочим.
Может быть.
Хозяин и не сделал бы ей предложение.
Вот ваш чек.
А вы знаете, сколько этот коньяк стоит?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Я подумал.
'I thought about it.' Kristina brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'would think' in a few short words.
Дело же не в нем.
'It is not really about the ring.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'matter', while 'him' completes the thought. Kristina answers right away.
Давай выпьем за нас.
'Let us drink to the two of us.' In Russian, the idea of 'let's' flows naturally into 'us' without extra filler words.
За нас?
'To the two of us?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'behind' before landing on 'us'.
До дна.
'Bottoms up.' The grammar packs 'until' and 'bottom' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Что это был косяк.
'That it was a blunder at all.' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'hers' in spoken Russian.
Потому что вся вселенная не хотела.
'Because the entire universe did not want it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'because' and 'to want' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Чтобы хозяин женился на этой стерве.
'For the owner to marry that shrew.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to marry', turning the action back on the subject. Kristina answers right away.
А я сейчас серьезно говорю, между прочим.
'And I am speaking completely seriously right now, by the way.' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'other' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Может быть.
'Perhaps.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'maybe', while 'maybe' completes the thought.
Хозяин и не сделал бы ей предложение.
'The owner never would have proposed to her.' In Russian, the idea of 'owner' flows naturally into 'offer' without extra filler words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Вот ваш чек.
'Here is your bill.' In Russian, the idea of 'there you go' flows naturally into 'receipt' without extra filler words.
А вы знаете, сколько этот коньяк стоит?
'Do you have any idea how much this cognac costs?' Kristina brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'you' in a few short words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
